report.summary: Chunk 2 of 5: source scanning utilities including _Src dataclass, AST helpers for import analysis, dispatch chains, branch literals, and shim detection. All docstring claims checked; some are uncheckable due to missing definitions or incomplete function. Observations note minor redundancy and incomplete function.
risks: _walk | low | _walk imports os inside the function despite module-level import; redundant but harmless. | Remove the inner import.
_shim_body | medium | _shim_body is incomplete; the chunk ends mid-function, so behavior is unknown. | Review the full function in the next chunk.
_toplevel_names | low | _toplevel_names does not descend into For/While loops; may miss names bound inside loops that always execute. | Consider if such patterns exist in the codebase.

handoff.purpose: Source scanning helpers: _Src dataclass, AST utilities for import analysis, dispatch chains, branch literals, shim detection.

symbols.name: _Src
symbols.note: Mutable scratch for one parsed module, never escapes analyse.

symbols.name: _py_dotted
symbols.note: Converts relative path to dotted module name.

symbols.name: _iter_py
symbols.note: Yields sorted list of .py files under root.

symbols.name: _walk
symbols.note: Wrapper around os.walk with directory filtering.

symbols.name: _is_main_guard
symbols.note: Checks if an AST node is an if __name__ == '__main__' guard.

symbols.name: _branch_literals
symbols.note: Extracts string literals from branch conditions.

symbols.name: _dispatch_chains
symbols.note: Finds if/elif chains with enough branches to be dispatch tables.

symbols.name: _is_never_true
symbols.note: Checks if a test is a constant False/0.

symbols.name: _catches_import_error
symbols.note: Checks if a try statement catches ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError.

symbols.name: _split_imports
symbols.note: Splits imports into live and weak records based on context.

symbols.name: _import_records_of
symbols.note: Returns only live import records from an AST node.

symbols.name: _toplevel_names
symbols.note: Returns names bound at module level, descending into conditionals.

symbols.name: _module_level_bindings
symbols.note: Maps names bound by module-level imports to their import records.

symbols.name: _shim_body
symbols.note: Detects if a module body is a pure re-export shim.

claims.why: The claim refers to a function 'analyse' not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: String literals a branch condition selects on.
claims.why: The function extracts string literals from Compare, BoolOp, and Call with startswith/endswith.

claims.text: Covers the two shapes real dispatch chains use: ``x == "literal"`` and ``x.startswith("/api/")``
claims.why: The function handles Compare (x == literal) and Call with startswith/endswith.

claims.text: A branch we cannot read contributes nothing rather than a guess.
claims.why: The function returns an empty list for unrecognized patterns; no fallback guessing.

claims.text: Flat if/elif chains inside one function, as (literal, node) pairs.
claims.why: The function collects chains of if/elif and pairs each literal with the if node.

claims.text: A chain is only a command table when it is long enough (``_MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES``); shorter ones are ordinary conditionals and reporting them as subcommands would fabricate entry points.
claims.why: The constant _MIN_DISPATCH_BRANCHES is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``if False:`` / ``if 0:`` -- a branch the interpreter deletes.
claims.why: The function checks for ast.Constant with falsy value (False, 0, etc.).

claims.text: Deliberately literal-only. Inferring that some NAME is falsy would make the walk guess, and a guess in this direction silently deletes real edges.
claims.why: The function only checks ast.Constant, not Name nodes.

claims.text: Does this ``try`` swallow a failing import?
claims.why: The function checks if any handler type names ImportError or ModuleNotFoundError.

claims.text: Narrow on purpose: only handlers that NAME ImportError (or ModuleNotFoundError) count. A bare ``except Exception`` around an import is usually a lazy-optional-dependency idiom too, but widening this rule reclassifies real edges on evidence that is not there.
claims.why: The function only matches ast.Name or ast.Attribute with id/attr in _IMPORT_ERRORS; bare Exception is not matched.

claims.text: (live records, [(weak record, why)]) for one subtree.
claims.why: The function returns a tuple of (list of live records, list of (record, why) tuples).

claims.text: Structural descent rather than ``ast.walk`` because the whole point is the CONTEXT an import sits in: the same statement is evidence in one branch and not in another.
claims.why: The function uses a recursive helper 'rec' that traverses child nodes manually, not ast.walk.

claims.text: LIVE import records only. Weak ones are reachable only via :func:`_split_imports`, so no caller can pick them up by accident.
claims.why: The function calls _split_imports and returns only the first element (live records).

claims.text: Names a module binds at import time. Descends one level into ``if`` and ``try`` because conditional definitions are ordinary in this codebase.
claims.why: The function descends into If, Try, With, AsyncWith handlers up to depth 3.

claims.text: Name bound by a MODULE-LEVEL import -> the record that bound it.
claims.why: The function iterates over module-level statements and maps bound names to import records.

claims.text: MODULE LEVEL ONLY, and that restriction is load-bearing.
claims.why: The function only iterates over tree.body (module-level statements) and does not recurse into nested scopes.

claims.text: True when the module body re-exports and does nothing else.
claims.why: The function is incomplete in this chunk; the full logic is not visible.

claims.text: Detected structurally, never guessed: no def, no class, no executable statement beyond imports, ``__all__`` and plain alias assignments.
claims.why: The function is incomplete; the check for def/class/executable statements is not fully shown.

observations.what: _walk function uses os.walk but also imports os inside the function; the import is redundant given the module-level import.
_shim_body is incomplete; the function body ends abruptly after a comment and an if statement, suggesting the chunk cut off.
_toplevel_names descends into If, Try, With, AsyncWith but not into other control flow like For or While; this may miss names bound inside loops that are guaranteed to execute.
